When a UAS, designed for conventional take-off and landing on a runway is equipped with an automatic taxi system, it must meet the following requirements:
(a) Taxi
  (1) Before the automatic taxi mode can be engaged the system must provide to the UAS operator a clear and deterministic indication of the taxi path and planned speed that will be automatically followed.
  (2) Once the automatic taxi mode has been engaged, the UA steering, speed and braking are fully automatic until the UA reaches full stop or the UAS crew provides manual inputs into the automatic taxi settings, or changes to a manual taxi mode. UA taxi path, speed, configuration, engine settings, steering and braking during taxi are controlled by the automatic taxi system.
  (3) In case of failure that could adversely affect safe taxi, or exceeding of predefined limits occurring during the taxi, or a failure in the communication control link, an automatic abort function shall be provided to stop the UA.
(b) The automatic system must incorporate a manual abort function. Its control shall be easily accessible to the UAS crew in order to stop the UA during all automated taxi operations on the taxiway or runway.
